children: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL, Financials), the parent company of Google, is securing more round-the-clock electricity for its expanding data-center footprint through a new geothermal agreement with Fervo Energy.
Fervo said it will supply Google with 396 megawatts of geothermal power from its Cape Station project in Utah.
The agreement also gives Google an option to purchase roughly 600 megawatts more, potentially taking total capacity under the arrangement to nearly 1 gigawatt by June 2030.
Fervo shares jumped nearly 14% in premarket trading following the announcement. For Google investors, the bigger story is the scale of the power commitment.
AI data centers require enormous amounts of reliable electricity, pushing technology companies to secure generation years before new facilities come online.
Geothermal power offers an advantage because it can generate electricity around the clock rather than depending on weather conditions.

Google and Fervo already have a relationship. In 2024, Fervo signed a 115-megawatt power purchase agreement with Google and NV Energy after the companies began working together on Project Red in Nevada.
Cape Station is expected to begin operating in 2028 and is intended to support potential Google data-center development in Utah.
The nearly 1-gigawatt option shows how aggressively Google is planning for future AI power requirements.

title: Google Just Locked In Nearly 1 Gigawatt of Geothermal Power
